reference_title: Design and Construction of Driven Pile Foundations

sections.title: Overview of Plan and Specification Requirements
sections.summary: Piles cannot be inspected after installation, so plans and specifications matter. Plans should show pile locations and numbering, type, section and estimated length, toe details, splices, cutoff elevation, cap connection, estimated and minimum toe elevations, batter, H-pile orientation, Rr, Rn, Rndr, and boring locations and results. A bare '300 kips' is ambiguous: state the factored resistance, resistance factor, nominal resistance, unsuitable layer resistance, setup or relaxation, and Rndr.
sections.body: 14.1 (pp. 281-283): plans, details and specifications for piling are the foundation designer's responsibility with materials and construction personnel. Plans should include: pile locations; a numbering system; pile type, section and estimated length; toe details (driving shoe, closure plate); splicing details; cutoff elevation; cap connection details; estimated toe elevation; minimum toe elevation if needed; batter and direction; H-pile orientation; factored resistance Rr; nominal resistance Rn; nominal driving resistance Rndr; boring locations and exploration results. The designer must use compatible language, especially for Rndr; problems arise when plans give only one resistance without the resistance factor of the control method or losses from scour, liquefaction or relaxation. 'Piles shall have a resistance of 300 kips' could mean Rr, Rn or Rndr; plans should state the factored resistance, resistance factor, nominal resistance, resistance of unsuitable layers (scour, liquefaction and their elevations), setup or relaxation, and the resulting Rndr. The generic specification (FHWA Geotechnical Guideline 13, updated from ASD to LRFD; AASHTO (2010) construction specifications are similar) needs agency review before use, includes commentary, and covers driven piles only. Design-bid-build uses agency standard specifications (agency takes the risk); design-build uses performance specifications (design-builder takes the risk); CM/GC uses standard specifications. Table 14-1 lists items to include.
key_points: Piles cannot be inspected after installation; specifications and monitoring are of prime importance
Plans: locations, numbering, type, section, estimated length, toe details, splices, cutoff, cap connection, toe elevations, batter
Plans must give factored resistance Rr, nominal resistance Rn and nominal driving resistance Rndr
A bare '300 kips' is ambiguous; state resistance factor, unsuitable layers, setup or relaxation, and Rndr
Generic specification from FHWA Geotechnical Guideline 13, updated to LRFD; needs agency review
Design-bid-build: agency takes the risk; design-build: design-builder takes the risk

tables.title: Items to Include in a Driven Pile Specification
tables.description: Pile materials (type, grade, strength; coatings; transportation and handling); driving system and equipment (hammer, hammer and pile cushions, helmet and inserts, leads, followers, predrilling, jetting, spudding); installation (sequence, location and alignment tolerances, shoes, splices, cutoff, cap connection, heave, rejection criteria); resistance verification (static, dynamic, rapid load testing, wave equation, dynamic formulas); basis of payment.

sections.applicability: What driven pile plans must show and how to state required resistances.

sections.title: Generic Driven Pile Specification
sections.summary: A generic driven pile specification (pp. 284-330) in eight sections: X.01 Description, X.02 Submittals and Approvals, X.03 Materials, X.04 Driving Equipment and Appurtenances, X.05 Determination of Nominal Resistance, X.06 Preparation and Driving, X.07 Method of Measurement and X.08 Basis of Payment.
sections.body: 14.2 (pp. 284-330): a generic driven pile specification in eight sections, opening with its own contents list (pp. 284-285). Section X.01 Description (p. 286). Section X.02 Submittals and Approvals (p. 287): the pile installation plan, and approval of the pile driving equipment by wave equation or by an alternate method. Section X.03 Materials (p. 295). Section X.04 Driving Equipment and Appurtenances (p. 296): pile hammers, and the drive system components and accessories (hammer cushion, helmet, pile cushion, leads, followers, jets, predrilling equipment, spuds). Section X.05 Determination of Nominal Resistance (p. 303): axial compression by static load test, dynamic testing with signal matching, rapid load test, wave equation analysis or dynamic formula; axial tension by static load test or dynamic testing with signal matching; lateral resistance by static load test. Section X.06 Preparation and Driving (p. 316): site work, preparation of piling, and driving (test, probe and indicator piles, production piles, driving stress, installation sequence, tolerances, heaved piles, obstructions, refusal, splices, cutoffs, unsatisfactory piles). Section X.07 Method of Measurement (p. 325). Section X.08 Basis of Payment (p. 329).
key_points: Eight specification sections, X.01 Description to X.08 Basis of Payment (pp. 286-330)
Driving equipment is approved by wave equation analysis or by an alternate method (Section X.02)
Nominal resistance: compression by static, dynamic, rapid load test, wave equation or dynamic formula; tension by static or dynamic test; lateral by static load test (Section X.05)
sections.applicability: The layout of a generic driven pile specification and where each provision sits.

subsections.title: Section X.01 Description and Section X.02 Submittals and Approvals
subsections.summary: Test pile results set production lengths. A Pile Installation Plan is due 30 days before the first pile. Equipment is approved by wave equation unless a dynamic formula is specified: 30 to 96 bl/ft at the required resistance and stresses within limits (phi_da 1.0, timber 1.15): steel 0.90 fy; prestressed tension 0.095 sqrt(f'c) + fpe, or fpe in severe environments; compression 0.85 f'c - fpe; timber 2.6 Fco. For formula projects the alternate method uses minimum rated energies (Table 14-3) and at most 10 blows/in.
subsections.body: X.01 (p. 286): furnish and drive piles of the designated type and dimensions; with test piles, plan lengths are estimates and the Engineer sets production lengths after testing; the contractor adds length for fresh heading without compensation. Commentary: the owner estimates lengths and contractors should not be penalized for inaccurate estimates. X.02 A (pp. 287-288): the Pile Driving Installation Plan, due 30 days before the first pile, lists equipment (with hammer data sheets), field hammer energy methods and calibrations, follower and template drawings, load test equipment and calibrations, driving sequence, schedule, preconstruction surveys of nearby structures and utilities, shop drawings, measures against pile movement during fill within 15 ft, reinforcement and concrete placement in pipe piles, batter pile support, and splice details. X.02 B (pp. 288-293): equipment approved by wave equation unless a formula is specified; none brought to site before written approval; the Pile and Driving Equipment Data Form (Figure 14-1) due 30 days before driving, and submitted even when the wave equation is not used. Criteria: 30 to 96 bl/ft at the required resistance (below practical refusal of 10 blows/in.) and stresses within limits with phi_da 1.0 (timber 1.15): steel compression 0.90 of minimum yield; prestressed tension 0.095 sqrt(f'c) + fpe (ksi) in normal and fpe in severe corrosive environments; prestressed compression 0.85 f'c - fpe; timber compression 2.6 Fco. Response in 14 calendar days, revisions in 7; no changes without written approval and no time extension for revisions. Commentary: Rndr includes unsuitable, liquefiable and scour zone resistance, minimum penetration, driving gains or losses and jetting or predrilling effects; show it on the plans; optimum driving is below the bearing graph's maximum curvature, typically 84 to 96 bl/ft (Table 14-2 factors; none for rapid load tests). X.02 C (pp. 294-295): when a formula controls, hammers must meet the rated energies of Table 14-3 and the formula blow count must not exceed 10 blows/in.; agencies build the table from wave equation analyses (too large: stress problems or under 30 bl/ft; too small: over 120 bl/ft) for routine projects in uniform soils only.
key_points: Pile Driving Installation Plan due 30 days before driving the first pile
No driving equipment to site before written approval; data form (Figure 14-1) due 30 days before driving
Wave equation approval: 30 to 96 bl/ft at the required nominal resistance, below 10 blows/in. practical refusal
phi_da = 1.0 for all pile types except timber (1.15)
Steel: compression <= phi_da x 0.90 x minimum yield strength
Prestressed concrete tension: phi_da (0.095 sqrt(f'c) + fpe) normal; phi_da fpe severe corrosive (ksi)
Prestressed concrete compression: phi_da (0.85 f'c - fpe); timber: phi_da x 2.6 Fco
Engineer responds within 14 calendar days, revisions within 7
Rndr includes resistance of unsuitable, liquefiable and scour zone soils; show it on the plans
Alternate (formula) approval: minimum rated energy by resistance (Table 14-3), at most 10 blows/in.

tables.title: Resistance Factors for Field Determination Methods
tables.description: AASHTO compression phi_dyn: static load test on at least one pile per site condition plus dynamic testing with signal matching of at least two piles per site condition, not less than 2% of production piles, 0.80; static load test without dynamic testing 0.75; dynamic testing with signal matching on 100% of production piles 0.75; dynamic testing of at least two piles per site condition, not less than 2%, 0.65; wave equation alone at end of drive 0.50; FHWA modified Gates 0.40; Engineering News 0.10. Tension: static load test 0.60; dynamic testing with signal matching 0.50.

tables.title: Alternate Approval Method Minimum Pile Hammer Requirements
tables.description: Minimum manufacturer's rated hammer energy (ft-lbs) by nominal resistance bands of 180 kips and under, 181-300, 301-420, 421-540, 541-600 and over 600 kips; the energy column is left blank for each agency to fill from wave equation analyses (see commentary).

subsections.applicability: Contractor submittals and driving equipment approval in a driven pile specification.

subsections.title: Section X.03 Materials and Section X.04 Driving Equipment and Appurtenances
subsections.summary: Materials follow agency standard specifications. Hammers: air, steam, diesel or hydraulic; drop hammers only if permitted, not for concrete piles or resistance over 120 kips, ram at least 2.0 kips and the helmet plus pile weight, drop at most 12 ft. Stroke and energy must be observable for each hammer type. Vibratory production piles need a load test or impact restrike, and every tenth pile restruck. Durable hammer cushions; concrete pile cushions at least 4 in. with a formula, new for each pile.
subsections.body: X.03 (pp. 295-296): concrete, reinforcing, prestressing, structural steel, shoe castings, shells, timber, preservative and coatings per agency standard specifications. X.04 A (pp. 296-298): drop hammers, if permitted, not for concrete piles or above 120 kips, ram at least 2.0 kips and not less than helmet plus pile, drop at most 12.0 ft, with guides. Air/steam hammers within manufacturer ranges with accessible gauges; striking parts at least one third of helmet plus pile and at least 2.75 kips, waived with wave equation approval. Open-end diesels: stroke rings, a stroke vs blows per minute chart and an automatic stroke display. Closed-end diesels: bounce chamber gauge near ground and a chart calibrated within 60 days. Hydraulic hammers: kinetic energy or impact velocity display. Vibratory hammers only after the toe elevation is set by load testing or impact restrike of test piles (contractor's cost), controlled by power, penetration rate or toe elevation, with the first of every 10 piles restruck. Commentary: give inspectors hammer manuals; consider energy readouts (Section 15.19); no formula predicts vibratory resistance. X.04 B (pp. 298-302): hammer cushions of durable manufactured material (no wood, wire rope or asbestos) with a striker plate, inspected at each structure or every 100 hours and replaced if over 25% thinner; helmets guided by the leads, timber helmet at most 2.0 in. larger than the head; concrete pile cushions of plywood or hardwood, thickness by wave equation (at least 4 in. with a formula), new for each pile, replaced if compressed over half or burning, used cushions for restrike (cushions may exceed 18 in.; harden after 1000 to 1500 blows; under 50 blows unsuitable for restrike); fixed or swinging leads; followers only if approved, by wave equation, steel follower area at least 20% of a concrete pile, impedance 50 to 200% for steel or timber, first two piles checked, resistance verified by testing; jets removed 5 ft above the minimum toe, then impact driven; predrilling and spuds as specified.
key_points: Drop hammers: not for concrete piles or above 120 kips; ram >= 2.0 kips and >= helmet plus pile; drop <= 12 ft
Air/steam striking parts >= 1/3 of helmet plus pile and >= 2.75 kips (waived with wave equation approval)
Open-end diesel: stroke rings, stroke-blow rate chart, automatic stroke display
Closed-end diesel: bounce chamber gauge and chart calibrated within 60 days; hydraulic: energy display
Vibratory: toe elevation set by load test or impact restrike; first of every 10 piles restruck
Hammer cushion: no wood, wire rope or asbestos; inspect every 100 hours, replace if 25% thinner
Concrete pile cushion: at least 4 in. with a formula; new each pile; replace if compressed half or burning
Followers: wave equation; steel area >= 20% of concrete pile; impedance 50-200% for steel or timber piles
Jets removed 5 ft above the minimum toe elevation; final driving with an impact hammer
subsections.applicability: Hammer, cushion, lead, follower, jetting and predrilling requirements in a driven pile specification.

subsections.title: Section X.05 Determination of Nominal Resistance
subsections.summary: Compression: static load tests (ASTM D1143 quick test, 150% of nominal resistance, failure by Eq 14-1 for piles 24 in. or less, Eq 14-2 over 36 in., interpolated between, at least 5 days after driving), dynamic testing with signal matching (restrike after up to 24 hours or per Table 14-4, warm hammer, 3 in. or 20 blows), rapid load tests, wave equation, or the Gates formula (Eqs 14-3 to 14-5, not over 600 kips). Tension: ASTM D3689 with Eq 14-6, or signal matching shaft resistance. Lateral: ASTM D3966 to 200% of design load.
subsections.body: A1 Static load tests (pp. 303-305): ASTM D1143 quick test to plunging failure or system capacity, loading system for 150% of nominal resistance, load cell and spherical bearing plate; PE-prepared apparatus plans, calibrations within 30 days; reaction piles of the production type, redriven if they rise 0.25 in. or more; failure by Eq 14-1 (24 in. or less) or Eq 14-2 (over 36 in.), interpolated for 24 to 36 in.; more than 1/4 in. of heave may require redriving; at least 5 days after driving. Commentary: wait at least 2 weeks in clays and shales, 5 days to a week in sandy silts and sands; measure toe load; jack gauges read 10 to 20% high from ram friction. A2 Dynamic testing (pp. 305-309): ASTM D4945; signal matching at end of driving and each restrike; personnel rated on the PDCA/PDI proficiency test; test at least half the reaction piles and the load test pile; from 2 piles per site condition (at least 2%) to 100%; gages 2 to 3 diameters below the head, about 1 hour per pile, 4 x 4 ft manlift, power and an 8 x 8 ft shelter as needed; stresses held within X.02 B limits; restrike after up to 24 hours (or Table 14-4), hammer warmed with at least 20 blows, at most 3 in. or 20 blows. A3 Rapid load tests (pp. 309-310): ASTM D7383; peak force above nominal plus dynamic resistance, above 50% of peak for 4L/C and above the pre-load for at least 12L/C (less with extra gages); transducer 10% above target; interpretation names its rate factor; no AASHTO resistance factor; at least 5 days after driving. A4 Wave equation (p. 311): penetration resistance reached within 5 ft of the estimated toe elevation. A5 Dynamic formula (pp. 311-313): only if the contract says so, not above 600 kips, not with damaged heads or followers; Gates Eqs 14-3 to 14-5; FHWA recommends minimizing formulas. B Tension (pp. 313-315): ASTM D3689 quick test to 150%, failure by Eq 14-6 times phi_up, or restrike signal matching shaft resistance times phi_up. C Lateral (pp. 315-316): ASTM D3966 standard procedure to 200% of design lateral load, deflection vs depth by inclinometers or a ShapeAccelArray.
key_points: Static compression test: ASTM D1143 quick test; loading system for 150% of nominal resistance; load cell required
Eq 14-1 (24 in. or less): sf = delta + (0.15 + b/120); Eq 14-2 (over 36 in.): sf = delta + b/30; interpolate between
Static test at least 5 days after driving; commentary: 2 weeks in clays and shales
Reaction piles rising 0.25 in. or more are redriven; test pile heave over 1/4 in. may require redriving
Jack pressure gauges commonly read 10-20% high; use a load cell
Dynamic test restrike after up to 24 hours (or Table 14-4); warm hammer 20 blows; at most 3 in. or 20 blows
Rapid load test: force above 50% of peak for 4L/C and above pre-load for 12L/C; at least 5 days after driving
Wave equation: penetration resistance reached within 5 ft of estimated toe elevation
Formula (Gates, Eqs 14-3 to 14-5) not above 600 kips, not with damaged heads or followers
Tension: Eq 14-6 sf = delta + 0.15 times phi_up, or signal matching shaft resistance times phi_up
Lateral: ASTM D3966 to 200% of design lateral load with deflection vs depth

tables.title: Common Time Delay for Restrike Based Upon Soil Type
tables.description: Restrike delay by soil type: clean sands 1 day; silty sands 2 days; sandy silts 3-5 days; silty clays 7-14 days; shales 10-14 days (longer times sometimes required for the last two).

subsections.applicability: Specifying how nominal resistance is verified in compression, tension and lateral loading.

subsections.title: Section X.06 Preparation and Driving, Section X.07 Method of Measurement, and Section X.08 Basis of Payment
subsections.summary: Excavate before driving and finish abutment fill settlement first. Test piles short of Rndr 1 ft above estimated toe set up 12 to 24 hours. Groups are driven from the center outward or across from an outside row. Tolerances: 1:50 vertical, 1:25 batter, 6 in. (3 in. for bents), cutoff +1.5/-4 in. Heave redrive over 0.25 in. (end bearing) or 1.5 in. (shaft). Practical refusal 10 blows/in. for 3 inches; absolute 20 blows for 1 in. or less. Separate pay items split fixed from variable costs.
subsections.body: X.06 A (pp. 316-318): excavate to grade where practical; place abutment fill and let settlement finish first; fill predrilled voids with sand; no spuds in lieu of predrilling without approval; stop predrilling at least 5 ft above the plan toe except for end bearing on rock or hardpan; predrill through fills over 5 ft thick with holes no larger than the pile's greatest dimension plus 6 in. B (pp. 318-319): plane heads, strands cut below the surface, chamfered concrete and timber heads; timber collars above 200 kips; cast steel shoes (ASTM A148 Grade 90-60), A36 closure plates; welded plate H-pile shoes not recommended; mark piles every foot with cumulative distance every 5 ft. C (pp. 319-325): test piles with the approved system; if Rndr is not reached 1 ft above the estimated toe, set up 12 to 24 hours and redrive with a warm hammer (20 blows); order list within 7 days. Production piles to resistance, resistance and minimum toe, or toe elevation, with blow counts and hammer performance recorded; jetted and vibratory piles judged by impact driving; follower criteria checked by testing. Group sequence from the center outward or from an outside row across. Tolerances: 0.25 in./ft (1:50) vertical, 0.5 in./ft (1:25) batter; head within 6 in. (3 in. for bents); at least 4 in. from the cap edge; cutoff 1.5 in. above to 4 in. below; embedment at least 8 in. Heave: redrive end bearing piles over 0.25 in. and shaft piles over 1.5 in. Practical refusal 10 blows/in. for at most 3 consecutive inches; absolute refusal 20 blows for 1 in. or less; on hard rock 5 blows per 1/4 in. or 10 per 1/2 in. No timber splices; steel splices per AWS D1.1. Treated timber cutoffs get copper naphthenate (2% copper). A concrete pile with a crack around its whole periphery is defective; misaligned piles are not forced into position. X.07 (pp. 325-329): mobilization 75% when satisfactory driving starts and 25% at completion; furnished and driven piles separate; splices only beyond plan lengths. X.08 (pp. 329-330): Table 14-5.
key_points: Abutment fill placed and settlement complete before driving
Predrilling stops at least 5 ft above plan toe except end bearing on rock or hardpan
Test piles short of Rndr 1 ft above estimated toe: set up 12 to 24 hours, redrive with a warm hammer
Group sequence: center outward, or from an outside row progressively across
Tolerances: 1:50 vertical, 1:25 batter; head 6 in. (3 in. bents); cutoff +1.5/-4 in.; embedment >= 8 in.
Heave: redrive end bearing piles over 0.25 in., shaft piles over 1.5 in.
Practical refusal 10 blows/in. for at most 3 consecutive inches; absolute refusal 20 blows for 1 in. or less
Hard rock: absolute refusal 5 blows per 1/4 in. or 10 blows per 1/2 in.
No timber pile splices; concrete pile with a full-periphery crack is defective
Mobilization paid 75% at start of satisfactory driving, 25% at completion
Separate pay items split fixed costs (mobilization, splices, shoes) from length-dependent costs

tables.title: Basis of Payment
tables.description: Pay units: mobilization and demobilization lump sum; piles and test piles furnished and driven per linear foot or each; static, rapid and lateral load tests, dynamic pile tests (during driving, during restrike), splices, shoes and pile cutoffs (over 5 ft lengths only) each; predrilling and jetting per linear foot or each; spudding and delays per hour.
